newsitem.title: HONG KONG: China tells Britain PLA troops for HK defence only.
newsitem.headline: China tells Britain PLA troops for HK defence only.

text.p: China assured Britain on Monday that its new military garrison in Hong Kong would be involved only in external defence.
British officials said Foreign Secretary Robin Cook won this pledge in a 45-minute meeting with Chinese Foreign Minister Qian Qichen.

The arrival of the PLA troops, from three hours before the midnight handover ceremony, has stirred anxiety over potential military action against civilians, like Beijing's 1987 crushing of student-led democracy protesters.
Qian's response was in line with previous pledges that Hong Kong's internal security would be left to local police.
Cook underlined Britain's regret at the scale of China's troop deployment, involving a land, air and sea sweep by 4,000 troops, and said he did not see a need for armoured vehicles.

British officials said Cook sought assurances from Qian that China would keep to the terms of the 1984 Sino-British joint declaration under which internal security was the responsibility of Hong Kong police.
"He received the assurances that he was seeking about the PLA," a British official said after the meeting described as friendly.
Cook told Qian that Britain was looking for a fresh start in relations and Hong Kong should act as a bridge.
He voiced concern about the dissolution of Hong Kong's elected assembly and called for "free and fair elections" as early as possible.
British officials said Qian told him he was confident polls would be held before June 30 next year.
